name: Osteoblastoma
definition: Rare benign osteoblastic tumor larger than osteoid osteoma, often arising in posterior elements of the spine and capable of causing pain or neurological compression.

investigations.principle: CT defines mineralized lesion; MRI assesses neural/soft-tissue extension; biopsy may be required.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Surgical excision or ablation strategy depends on size, site and neural proximity.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi-granthi phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Rare benign osteoblastic tumor larger than osteoid osteoma, often arising in posterior elements of the spine and capable of causing pain or neurological compression.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
